newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-FLUGELS HAT TRICK STOPS SIX-GAME RUN BY KASHIMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FLUGELS HAT TRICK STOPS SIX-GAME RUN BY KASHIMA.

text.p: Yokohama Flugels ended J.League first-stage leaders Kashima Antlers' six-game winning streak with 5-3 victory at home in a second-stage match on Saturday.

Japanese international midfielder Motohiro Yamaguchi scored a hat trick for the Flugels, opening the scoring after 25 minutes and then taking advantage of Kashima's sloppy defence for two more goals midway through the second half.

Hiroki Hattori and Brazilian international Sampaio knocked home vital first-half goals in Flugels' payback to the Antlers after being edged by Kashima in the first stage of the competition which ended last month.

Kashima's loss helped second-stage leaders Jubilo Iwata stretch the gap with a hard-fought 2-1 home win over bottom club Kobe, aided by first goals of the season by Kiyokazu Kudo and Norihisa Shimizu.

Iwata will be hoping to cling on to a perfect score of 15 points from five matches, five points clear of second-place Hiratsuka, who managed to gain one point by edging host Ichihara 6-5 on penalties after the two teams failed to break a scoreless deadlock in extra time.

Meanwhile, struggling two-time league champion Kawasaki took their first points of the stage against visitor Shimizu with a sudden-death goal one minute before the end of extra time by veteran midfielder Tsuyoshi Kitazawa.
Elsewhere, Gamba Osaka hammered Hiroshima 3-0 at home with one goal apiece for Shigeru Morioka, Nebojsa Krupnikovic and Masanobu Matsunami.
Fukuoka took its second straight victory with a 2-1 win at Urawa on goals by Nigerian Michael Obiku and Daisuke Nakaharai.
Brazilian midfielder Craudinho gave Cerezo Osaka a 1-0 victory at Kashiwa with a 76th-minute goal, while Yokohama Marinos downed Kyoto 4-1 in Friday's fixture.
